specs.scene: Overhead flatlay crowded to all four edges: a stack of printed payout summaries, a crumpled receipt, a domain renewal notice, a paper bank statement, a 1099 tax form, a coiled charging cable, the corner of a laptop keyboard, a handful of loose bills, a chipped coffee mug, a legal pad with a torn corner, a calculator, and a small stack of business cards, all overlapping with small bare patches of desk surface left between them, two hands entering from the bottom edge reaching toward the papers.
specs.source_quote: about seventy percent of micro-SaaS products never clear a thousand a month

recognisable.why: Scattered small-business paperwork reads as generic finance clutter, not a named brand or trade, though a few items (payout slips) hint at software income.

legibility.why: A dozen distinct objects must each be resolved separately, well past the two-element ceiling even accounting for the house layout's built-in density.

curiosity.why: The verdict phrase implies precarity but the viewer cannot see whether it is true from the objects alone, so some pull exists but it is muted by clutter.

subject.why: No single person mid-action or one distinctive object anchors the frame; it is a field of many small items.

credible.why: No figure is stated anywhere in the overlay, which scores full by the rubric's own rule.

stakes.why: Bills, tax forms and a coffee-ringed invoice directly imply financial strain the viewer could recognize as their own risk.

reexpress.why: Title carries the capital-indifference argument while the image supplies the lived consequence of barely covering costs, a genuine split.

specs.scene: A documentary photograph of a single suburban house shot straight-on at eye level in flat daylight, empty driveway, a neatly mowed lawn, a plain stretch of sky above the roofline, no people, no vehicles, all surfaces blank and unmarked.
specs.source_quote: That is not a scandal. It is the stated model, working as designed.

recognisable.why: A suburban house is an everyday physical object anyone recognizes, though it does not itself signal the software-economy topic without the title.

legibility.why: The house is the single focal mass in the frame with nothing else competing for resolution.

curiosity.why: The blunt verdict over an ordinary house implies a judgement the viewer cannot verify by looking, inviting the click to find out why.

subject.why: The house functions as one clear, distinctive object anchor for the frame.

credible.why: No number appears anywhere in the overlay, satisfying the full-credit rule for absence of a figure.

stakes.why: The loss is about a company's balance sheet, not a direct threat or gain to the viewer's own situation, so relevance is inferred rather than stated.

reexpress.why: The image supplies a concrete failure the title's abstract framing does not name, splitting the argument across image and title.

specs.scene: A single card-swipe payment reader sits alone on a plain countertop, angled slightly toward the camera and filling most of the frame, no hands, no packaging, no other objects, the background a flat, blank surface.
specs.source_quote: What protects you is not their incomprehension. It is their indifference.

recognisable.why: A card reader is an everyday physical object nearly every viewer has touched, scoring high even without a visible brand.

legibility.why: One object fills the frame with nothing else to resolve separately.

curiosity.why: The phrase implies a structural verdict about platform behavior that the object alone does not explain, prompting the click.

subject.why: The reader is a single, distinctive manufactured object serving as the frame's anchor.

credible.why: No figure appears in the overlay, which is full credit by the rubric's stated rule.

stakes.why: Implies the viewer's own transactions are taxed regardless of their size, a direct and personal financial stake.

reexpress.why: The title's mechanism argument is answered by the image's consequence — the toll applies no matter who you are — a real split rather than repetition.

specs.scene: A barber mid-cut in a small barbershop, gripping clippers against a client's neckline, framed close from the chest up with the client's face out of frame, a clean expanse of blank wall to the left, shop tools softly out of focus in the background.
specs.source_quote: Three decades of being profitable in one storefront is not a consolation prize

recognisable.why: A barber cutting hair is an instantly familiar trade requiring no explanation, the strongest possible recognisability.

legibility.why: One person performing one action forms a single focal mass even at small size.

curiosity.why: The overlay states a plain description rather than an unresolved judgement, leaving little for the viewer to want to verify.

subject.why: A person mid-action is a clear, unambiguous human anchor.

credible.why: No figure is carried in the overlay, earning full credit by the stated rule.

stakes.why: Implies a shift in how software workers might live and earn, a moderate personal relevance rather than a sharp threat.
